body.text: Overview and Empirical Foundations of Day trading

Day trading is a share trading strategy in which a trader buys and sells the same financial instrument or security on the same trading day. As can be seen on the chart on the right, the price of stock can vary somewhat in the course of the day, and the point at which the buy and sell transactions take place will determine whether the trader makes a profit or loss, taking into account any fees on the transactions. The day trader will normally close all positions (i.e. sells all the securities) before the market closes on the trading day to avoid unmanageable risks and negative price gaps between one day's close and the next day's price at the open. Day traders are generally classified as speculators. Day trading contrasts with the long-term trades underlying buy-and-hold and value investing strategies. Day trading may require fast trade execution, sometimes as fast as milliseconds in scalping, therefore direct-access day trading software is often needed.
